issues.title: Register as "Reserved" all known labels that don't formally qualify
issues.author: robstradling
issues.body:
Some labels are recognized widely but (as far as we know) have no formal specification (e.g., DSA PRIVATE KEY and other labels listed at https://share.google/aimode/QHZsPU85tr3cyx637).

Other labels are specified but don't qualify for this registry (e.g., the two examples given in the document - ACME RESPONSE and SSH2 PUBLIC KEY).

Part of the purpose of this registry is to enable "specification authors...to avoid collisions".  It would be a "collision" of sorts, and would certainly generate confusion, if a future spec author decided to define a PEM label named (e.g.,) "ACME RESPONSE" with content that encapsulates a base64 (not base64url) encoded ACME response.

I think we could (should?) add to the registry as many of these widely recognized, non-qualifying labels as we can find, but mark them as "Reserved" rather than compatibly defined by a particular document.  It would be good to capture the reason for non-qualification, where known.  We would also need a way for a "Reserved" label to become qualified, in the event that missing documentation is either found or written (and there are no other reasons for non-qualification).

WDYT?

issues.title: Register new labels to support linting of PKI artifacts
issues.author: robstradling
issues.body:
Various PKI linting software, such as [pkilint](https://github.com/digicert/pkilint), is able to operate on a variety of PKI artifacts.  Often PEM input is accepted, but not all of those artifact types have corresponding PEM labels.

I think we should take this opportunity to register some new labels (in addition to "OCSP RESPONSE"), to support existing PKI linting use cases:
- TBS CERTIFICATE
- TBS CRL
- TBS OCSP RESPONSE

I think we should also register at least one label to support linting of Merkle Tree Certificates:
- TBS CERTIFICATE LOG ENTRY

comments.author: CBonnell
comments.body: I like this list. We might also want to consider registering `OCSP REQUEST`.
